text:
Owners seeking affiliation **without losing the hotel’s name, design, story, and local character** usually consider **soft brands or collection brands**. In Europe, the typical shortlist includes:

| Hotel group | Commonly considered collection brands | General positioning |
|---|---|---|
| **Marriott** | **Autograph Collection**, **Tribute Portfolio**, **The Luxury Collection**, **Design Hotels** | Premium through luxury; Design Hotels generally offers especially strong creative individuality |
| **Hilton** | **Tapestry Collection**, **Curio Collection**, **LXR Hotels & Resorts** | Upscale, upper-upscale and luxury respectively; designed to retain each property’s identity and story |
| **Accor** | **Handwritten Collection**, **MGallery Collection**, **Emblems Collection** | Midscale through luxury; particularly relevant given Accor’s extensive European platform |
| **IHG** | **Vignette Collection** | Luxury and lifestyle independent hotels with relatively light collection-level standards |
| **Hyatt** | **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt** | Upper-upscale and luxury properties seeking to maintain independence and individuality |
| **Radisson** | **Radisson Individuals**, including Premier and Boutique variants | Upscale to upper-upscale; strong European relevance and conversion flexibility |
| **Wyndham** | **Trademark Collection by Wyndham**, **Registry Collection Hotels** | Upper-midscale through luxury; intended for independently minded properties |
| **BWH Hotels** | **BW Premier Collection** and the various **WorldHotels** collections—Luxury, Elite, Crafted and Distinctive | Broad range, often attractive to owners wanting a lighter affiliation structure |

Marriott explicitly positions its collection brands as operating models for independent hotels, while Design Hotels uses an affiliation-oriented model for individually selected properties. ([hotel-development.marriott.com](https://www.hotel-development.marriott.com/brands/premium-brands?utm_source=openai))

Hilton’s Curio and Tapestry frameworks allow owners to preserve local character while accessing Hilton’s distribution, technology and loyalty platform; LXR addresses the luxury end of the independent-hotel market. ([stories.hilton.com](https://stories.hilton.com/releases/hiltons-curio-and-tapestry-collections-celebrate-200th-hotel-milestones?utm_source=openai))

Accor structures its collection portfolio by segment—Handwritten, MGallery and Emblems—with flexible standards intended to let the original hotel character remain visible. ([group.accor.com](https://group.accor.com/en/news-stories/collection-brands-handwritten-emblems-mgallery?utm_source=openai))

IHG, Hyatt and Radisson similarly emphasize retention of identity and individuality, with Radisson Individuals especially active as a European conversion option. ([ihgplc.com](https://www.ihgplc.com/our-brands/vignette?utm_source=openai))

**A practical first shortlist by segment would be:**

- **Midscale/upper-midscale:** Handwritten Collection, Trademark Collection  
- **Upscale:** Tapestry Collection, Radisson Individuals, BW Premier Collection  
- **Upper-upscale:** Autograph Collection, Tribute Portfolio, Curio Collection, MGallery, Unbound Collection  
- **Luxury:** Luxury Collection, LXR, Vignette Collection, Emblems Collection, Registry Collection, WorldHotels Luxury  
- **Maximum creative independence:** Design Hotels or a WorldHotels affiliation  

These brands still impose requirements covering quality, life safety, technology connectivity, loyalty participation and selected guest-experience standards. “Soft” therefore means **less prescriptive than a conventional chain brand**, not completely unrestricted. Wyndham, Radisson and WorldHotels explicitly describe their collection propositions as combining owner independence with group distribution and infrastructure. ([development.wyndhamhotels.com](https://development.wyndhamhotels.com/brand/trademark-collection-by-wyndham/?utm_source=openai))
